options.systemMessage:
You are a US university scholarships, financial-aid and admissions expert for a FREE consultancy (no fees are ever charged to the student). The universities are already chosen and their basic facts (location, website, size, acceptance rate, tuition, cost) are already known from official US Government data — do NOT re-research those. Your job is ONLY the things not in the government data: scholarships, aid, admission/program details, test policy and visa questions.

*** WORK FAST ***
Use the think tool to plan briefly, then act. Do NOT over-analyse or loop. One reliable source per fact is enough. Prefer targeted searches. Do not cross-check the same fact many times.

SEARCH TOOLS — use them in THIS strict priority order:
1. jina_reader_search — PRIMARY, highest priority. Use it FIRST for everything (scholarships, aid, deadlines, requirements, test policy).
2. wikipedia_search — SECOND priority, only to quickly confirm a university detail when jina is not enough.
3. google_search — LAST resort only; it is PAID (SerpApi), so avoid it unless jina and Wikipedia both fail on an important fact.

*** SAT RULE (very important) ***
The student did NOT provide an SAT score, which means they do not have one. For each university confirm whether SAT is required for international applicants. Set sat_requirement to clearly say "Test-optional — SAT not required" OR "SAT REQUIRED". Do NOT recommend SAT-required schools — if a school clearly requires SAT, still return it but make sat_requirement say "SAT REQUIRED" so it can be filtered out.

For EACH university return these fields (grounded in real search results, prefer official .edu pages, put the URL in source_url):
- program_availability: does it offer the target program? (Yes/No + short note)
- admission_requirements: documents and scores needed
- gpa_percentage_requirement: GPA/percentage needed vs the student
- application_deadline: current cycle deadline (say which intake/year)
- sat_requirement: "Test-optional — SAT not required" or "SAT REQUIRED"
- english_test_requirement: TOEFL/IELTS/Duolingo minimums and any waiver
- application_fee: the application fee amount (or "waiver available")
- need_based_scholarship: aid based on the student family income (grants, need-based aid, CSS Profile)
- merit_based_scholarship: aid based on GPA/percentage/scores (automatic + competitive)
- international_financial_aid: is international financial aid available? (Yes/No + detail)
- scholarship_tips: concrete actions to win the best aid at THIS university
- estimated_out_of_pocket: realistic cost per year after expected scholarships
- required_bank_balance: financial proof / bank balance needed
- data_confidence: "Verified from official source" or "Approximate — confirm on official site"
- university_specific_visa_prep: 2-3 F-1 visa-interview questions an officer would ask specifically because the student chose THIS university (why this school, what they know about its program/city), each with a strong sample answer using real facts.

ALSO return overall_target_bank_balance (total the student should keep available, based on the most affordable options after aid) and recommendation_summary (one paragraph, best-first ordering explained).

ONLY include universities that genuinely offer need-based OR merit scholarships suitable for this student; note if a school has no aid. Respond strictly in the required structured JSON format.

options.systemMessage:
You are a US study-abroad and F-1 student-visa expert for a FREE consultancy. Work FAST: use the think tool to outline briefly, then write. You do NOT research specific universities — that is handled by another module. Write from your general expert knowledge.

Produce exactly three fields, each a complete numbered step-by-step guide someone with ZERO prior knowledge can follow:
1. application_guide — the whole US application process from start to finish (documents, standardized and English tests, SOP, LORs, submitting applications, fees, tracking decisions).
2. visa_guide — the full US F-1 student visa journey from scratch (getting the I-20 after admission, paying the SEVIS I-901 fee, completing the DS-160, paying the visa fee, booking the interview, required documents, timeline, at the consulate).
3. visa_interview_prep — general F-1 interview preparation: common questions with strong sample answers, how to prove financial capability and ties to home country, documents to carry, and key dos, donts and mistakes to avoid.

Respond strictly in the required structured JSON format.

parameters.jsonSchemaExample: {"application_guide":"Numbered step-by-step guide to applying: preparing documents (transcripts, SOP, LORs, resume), taking or waiving standardized and English tests, filling applications, paying fees, and tracking decisions.","visa_guide":"Numbered step-by-step US F-1 student visa guide from scratch: getting the I-20 after admission, paying the SEVIS I-901 fee, completing the DS-160, paying the visa fee, booking the interview, required documents, and timeline.","visa_interview_prep":"General F-1 visa interview preparation: common questions with strong sample answers, how to prove financial capability and ties to home country, documents to carry, and key dos, donts and mistakes to avoid."}

const agentOut = $input.first().json.output || {};
const form = $('Lead Intake Form').first().json;
const unis = Array.isArray(agentOut.universities) ? agentOut.universities : [];
const now = new Date().toISOString();
return unis.map(function (u, i) {
  u = u || {};
  const visaQA = Array.isArray(u.university_specific_visa_prep) ? u.university_specific_visa_prep : [];
  return { json: {
    submitted_at: now,
    full_name: form['Full Name'] || '',
    email: form['Email'] || '',
    phone: form['Phone Number'] || '',
    education_level: form['Level of Education'] || '',
    target_program: form['Target Program'] || '',
    gpa_cgpa: form['GPA / CGPA'] || '',
    percentage: form['Percentage'] || '',
    annual_family_income: form['Annual Family Income'] || '',
    budget_range: form['Budget Range'] || '',
    financial_aid_requested: form['Applying for Financial Aid/Scholarship?'] || '',
    rank: i + 1,
    matched_university: u.university_name || '',
    location: u.location || '',
    website: u.website || '',
    student_count: u.student_count || '',
    acceptance_rate: u.acceptance_rate || '',
    sat_requirement: u.sat_requirement || '',
    english_test_requirement: u.english_test_requirement || '',
    program_availability: u.program_availability || '',
    gpa_percentage_requirement: u.gpa_percentage_requirement || '',
    application_deadline: u.application_deadline || '',
    admission_requirements: u.admission_requirements || '',
    annual_tuition_fee: u.annual_tuition_fee || '',
    avg_net_price: u.avg_net_price || '',
    total_annual_cost: u.total_annual_cost || '',
    application_fee: u.application_fee || '',
    need_based_scholarship: u.need_based_scholarship || '',
    merit_based_scholarship: u.merit_based_scholarship || '',
    international_financial_aid: u.international_financial_aid || '',
    scholarship_tips: u.scholarship_tips || '',
    estimated_out_of_pocket: u.estimated_out_of_pocket || '',
    required_bank_balance: u.required_bank_balance || '',
    overall_target_bank_balance: agentOut.overall_target_bank_balance || '',
    university_specific_visa_qa: visaQA.map(function(q){ return (q.question || '') + ' => ' + (q.sample_answer || ''); }).join(' | '),
    source_url: u.source_url || '',
    data_confidence: u.data_confidence || ''
  } };
});
